entries.name: Agentstools PII Redact
entries.description: Detect structured PII (emails, phones, credit cards, bank/tax ids, IPs, crypto addresses, secrets, etc.) in a text blob and return the sanitized text with each finding transformed — redact, mask, hash (salted SHA-256) or reversible tokenize — plus a findings report and GDPR/HIPAA/PCI compliance summary.

mode.description: Default transform applied to every entity (redact=type placeholder, mask=keep useful remainder, hash=salted SHA-256 so equal values stay linkable, tokenize=reversible replacement with a token map returned in the response)

entities.description: Optional allow-list of entity types to act on (default: all). See GET /pii/recognizers.

mode_overrides.description: Optional per-entity-type transform, keyed by type (e.g. mask phones but tokenize emails in one call)

salt.description: Optional salt mixed into hash mode

include_positions.description: Include character start/end offsets per finding

sanitized_text.description: The input text with every detected PII value transformed per the selected mode

compliance_categories.description: Counts of findings per compliance regime (GDPR, PCI, HIPAA, ...)

findings.description: Per-finding report (the raw PII value is NOT echoed back); with include_positions:true each finding also carries char start/end offsets

token_map.description: Only present in tokenize mode — maps each token back to its original value so the caller can restore it later (nothing is stored server-side)

usage.callShape: POST https://api.agentstools.dev/pii/redact with a JSON body: text (required — the text blob to sanitize) and mode (optional, default transform: redact|mask|hash|tokenize). Optional: entities[] (allow-list of entity types to act on — see GET /pii/recognizers), mode_overrides{} (per-entity-type transform), salt (mixed into hash mode), include_positions (bool — adds char offsets per finding). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 on Base (eip155:8453). Result is returned inline in the 200 body (synchronous, no poll).

inputExample.text: Email jane.doe@example.com, card 4111 1111 1111 1111.

usage.outputShape: {object:'pii_redact', mode, input_bytes, sanitized_text (the transformed text), summary{total_findings, counts_by_type{}, compliance_categories{GDPR,PCI,...}, has_pii}, findings[]{type, score, compliance_tags[], mode_applied} (+ char offsets when include_positions:true), findings_truncated, token_map{} (tokenize mode only), pack_version, disclaimer}
quirks: text is the only required field; mode defaults to redact if omitted. Four modes: redact (type placeholder like <EMAIL>), mask (keep a useful remainder e.g. card last-four), hash (salted SHA-256 so equal values stay linkable without exposure), tokenize (reversible — returns a token_map in the response body to restore later).
Fully STATELESS — tokenize returns the token map in the response and stores nothing server-side, so it is safe to run inside an agent pipeline.

Structured PII ONLY (emails, phones, credit cards, bank/tax ids, IPs, crypto addresses, secrets, etc.) via deterministic regex + checksum validators + a context boost; free-text person/org/location names (NER) are OUT OF SCOPE, so an empty findings list is NOT proof the text is PII-free.
The raw PII value is never echoed back in findings[]; each finding reports only type, score, compliance_tags and mode_applied (set include_positions:true to also get char start/end offsets).
Use entities[] to limit which types are touched and mode_overrides{} to vary the transform per type (e.g. mask phone numbers but tokenize emails in one call).
Indicators, not legal advice or a compliance guarantee — always review before relying on the result.
The transform companion to the sibling /pii/scan (detect-only, no transform) — that is a separate operation on the same host, not an alias of this one.

Read sanitized_text for the cleaned string, summary.has_pii / summary.counts_by_type / summary.compliance_categories for the headline, and findings[] for each hit ({type, score, compliance_tags, mode_applied}). Use mode='tokenize' when you need to restore the original later (the token_map is returned in the response — nothing is stored). Structured PII only — free-text names are out of scope; indicators, not legal advice. entries.name: Agentstools Match Name
entries.description: Fuzzy-match two names or addresses and return a 0-100 similarity score plus an is_match decision — normalizes legal forms, business stop-words, person titles and address abbreviations BEFORE fusing token, prefix (Jaro-Winkler), phonetic and edit similarity, so true matches like 'Acme Inc' vs 'ACME Incorporated' score high instead of falling below threshold.

type.description: Entity type selecting the normalization pipeline (default company).

min_score.description: Optional match threshold 0-100 (default is the per-type threshold).

a.description: First input echoed with its normalized form: {input, canonical, tokens[]}.

b.description: Second input echoed with its normalized form: {input, canonical, tokens[]}.

components.description: Per-component sub-scores: token_set, jaro_winkler, phonetic, edit.

threshold.description: The threshold used (per-type default or the supplied min_score).

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/match/name with query params: a (required — first string), b (required — second string), type (optional — person|company|address|product|org, default company, selects the normalization pipeline), min_score (optional integer 0-100 threshold override). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 JSON body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.01 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.

Verified live for a='Acme Inc', b='ACME Incorporated', type=company: score 100, is_match true, all four components 100, threshold 82, reasons ['normalized forms identical','same similarity_key (block candidates)'].
quirks: a and b are the only required params; type defaults to 'company' when omitted and selects the normalization pipeline (person strips titles/suffixes + maps nicknames; company canonicalizes legal forms + drops business stop-words; address folds USPS-style abbreviations).
Pure compute over the caller's own strings — no network, no keys, no storage.

The whole point is NORMALIZATION BEFORE MATCHING: a naive fuzzy ratio of 'Acme Inc' vs 'ACME Incorporated' is ~56 (below threshold), but canonicalizing the legal form first lifts a true match to ~100.
is_match is score >= threshold; pass min_score to override the per-type default threshold and re-rank with your own policy.
Similarity indicators for linkage/dedup, NOT authoritative identity resolution and NOT libpostal-grade international address parsing.

Distinct sibling ops on the same host: /match/key (blocking key, $0.005), /match/standardize (canonicalize one string, $0.005) and /match/dedupe (POST — dedupe a whole list into clusters, $0.02). /match/name is the pairwise two-string confirmer.

It normalizes legal forms, business stop-words, person titles and address abbreviations BEFORE the fuzzy compare, so 'Acme Inc' vs 'ACME Incorporated' scores 100 instead of ~56. entries.name: Agentstools Match Key
entries.description: Compute a deterministic similarity/blocking key for a single name or address — the cheap first step of client-side blocking and deduplication where records that share a key become duplicate candidates to confirm; normalizes legal forms, business stop-words, person titles and address abbreviations, then returns the key, the canonical form and the tokens.

value.description: The string to key (a name or address).

type.description: Entity type selecting the normalization pipeline (default company).

similarity_key.description: The deterministic blocking key; records sharing this key are duplicate candidates.

canonical.description: The normalized/canonical form of the input.

usage.callShape: GET https://api.agentstools.dev/match/key with query params: value (required — the string to key) and type (optional — person|company|address|product|org, default company, selects the normalization pipeline). No request body. Result is inline in the 200 JSON body (synchronous, no poll). Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 v2 on Base (eip155:8453), keyless.
usage.outputShape: JSON object: {object:'match_key', type, input, similarity_key, canonical, tokens[], phonetic_backend, pack_version, disclaimer}. Verified live for type=company, value='ACME Incorporated': similarity_key 'acme|#AKM', canonical 'acme', tokens ['acme'], phonetic_backend 'jellyfish.metaphone', pack_version '2026.07.12'.
quirks: value is the only required param; type defaults to 'company' when omitted and selects the normalization pipeline (person strips titles/suffixes; company canonicalizes legal forms + drops business stop-words; address folds USPS-style abbreviations).
Pure compute over the caller's own string — no network, no keys, no storage.

The similarity_key combines a token component and a phonetic (metaphone) component (e.g. 'acme|#AKM'); two records that produce the same key are candidate duplicates to confirm with a pairwise scorer.

This is a BLOCKING key generator, not a decision: use it to bucket a large list cheaply, then confirm candidate pairs with the sibling /match/name, or dedupe a whole list in one call with /match/dedupe.
Similarity indicators for linkage/dedup, NOT authoritative identity resolution and NOT libpostal-grade international address parsing.

Distinct sibling ops on the same host: /match/name (pairwise two-string score, $0.01), /match/standardize (canonicalize one string, $0.005) and /match/dedupe (POST — dedupe a whole list into clusters, $0.02). /match/key is the single-string blocking-key step.
usage.guide: Generate a deterministic blocking/similarity key for one name or address in a single keyless x402 call — the cheap first pass of large-scale dedup and record-linkage. GET https://api.agentstools.dev/match/key?value=<string>&type=<person|company|address|product|org> (type default company). Read similarity_key (records that share it are duplicate candidates), canonical (the normalized form) and tokens[]. Bucket a whole list by similarity_key first to avoid O(n^2) comparisons, then confirm candidate pairs with the sibling /match/name or cluster the whole list with /match/dedupe. Pure compute, no keys, no storage. Similarity indicators, not authoritative identity resolution. Pays $0.005 USDC via x402 on Base.
